title: Nevada County and FPPC to settle Measure V complaint - YubaNet
content: NEVADA CITY, Calif, August 10, 2026 – In November 2022 Nevada County voters rejected Measure V, a sales tax increase to be used for community-wide wildfire mitigation work. Nevada County sent two mailers to voters ahead of the election and a complaint was filed with the Fair Political Practices Commission (FPPC.) Today, an agreed settlement between FPPC’s Enforcement Division and Nevada County was published and provided to us from various sources. To resolve seven violations the stipulated agreement proposes, and Nevada County agreed to, a penalty of $31,500 will be paid by the county. The stipulation goes before the FPPC Commission on August 20, 2026 and the Commission can adopt or reject the order. Counts five to seven were added by the Enforcement Division once the determination was made that the mailers were campaign mailers, not informational only as the county stated. Be the first to know, sign up for our newsletter, absolutely free of course. A press release by the county reads, in part, “The County takes its obligations under the Political Reform Act seriously and is committed to ensuring compliance moving forward. The County has agreed to pay a discounted administrative penalty to resolve the case after four years in the FPPC process. The FPPC is expected to make a final determination on the agreement reached with the County at its Aug. 20 meeting.” The Enforcement Division recognized that “As part of the negotiated settlement, corrective campaign reports and statements have been filed now to provide full disclosure. Additionally, the County was cooperative during the investigation and exhibited intent to resolve the matter expeditiously.” Noteworthy is the fact that the Enforcement Division has very little latitude to lower penalties for local governments. title: Caitlin Clark injury update: Will the Fever star play v. NY Liberty? - marca.com
content: Caitlin Clark injury update: Will the Fever star play v. NY Liberty? The WNBA star's availability is not completely guaranteed for this high-stakes matchup. The Indiana Fever face a major test on Tuesday when they host the New York Liberty in a matchup that could significantly shape their playoff hopes. Heading into the game, the biggest question centered on Caitlin Clark’s health. The star guard has dealt with back soreness for much of the season, missing several games as a result and remaining a regular presence on the official injury report ever since. The news is encouraging for Indiana, however. The team listed Clark as “probable,” strongly indicating she will be available against the Liberty. The only new addition to the report is Grace VanSlooten, who is listed as “questionable” due to illness. Meanwhile, Damiris Dantas remains out after undergoing knee surgery that ended her season early. Another positive development for the Fever is the return of Aliyah Boston. The starting center is off the injury report for the first time in several weeks after recovering from a lower-leg issue. Clark has appeared in 28 games this season, averaging 21.6 points, 8.1 assists, 3.9 rebounds, and 1.0 steals per game—numbers that earned her a third consecutive WNBA All-Star selection. The timing could hardly be better for getting key pieces healthy. Indiana is entering the most demanding stretch of its schedule, with eight of its final 12 games against teams currently in playoff position. Before embarking on a five-game road trip, the Fever have two home opportunities to pick up wins. With such a challenging slate ahead, Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell will shoulder a large share of the offensive responsibility. If both continue performing at the level they’ve shown all season, Indiana will have a legitimate chance to stay in the playoff hunt. © 2026  Unidad Editorial Información Deportiva, S.L.U. title: Hybrid SUV faceoff: Comparing the Toyota RAV4 and Honda CR-V - USA Today
content: What is the RAV4's infotainment screen size compared to the CR-V Hybrid? How does the Jeep Cherokee's fuel economy compare to the RAV4 and CR-V? Why is the RAV4 more affordable than the CR-V Hybrid? Following Toyota’s decision to discontinue the gas RAV4 powertrain, the 2026 Toyota RAV4 will only be offered as a standard small hybrid SUV. One of its fiercest rivals in the 2026 Honda CR-V Hybrid. Both Japanese automakers produce practical family SUVs that deliver solid gas mileage thanks to electric motors. Here's how the RAV4 and CR-V Hybrid compare when it comes to pricing, specs standard features and more. The 2026 Toyota RAV4 is a completely redesigned compact SUV ushering in the nameplate's sixth generation. It introduces a new exterior styling, interior design and standard powertrain. Toyota's small hybrid SUV starts at $31,900. It uses a 2.5-liter four-cylinder engine and electric motors to produce 226 horsepower. The RAV4 achieves 47 miles per gallon in the city and 40 miles per gallon on the highway. It has stellar fuel economy for its segment and 37.8 cubic feet of cargo space. Toyota's small hybrid SUV is affordable, spacious enough for small families and has a long history of reliability. Honda still offers a gas version of its CR-V small SUV, but its hybrid iteration gets better gas mileage and delivers the same driving verve and handling that fans have come to love. Honda's CR-V Hybrid is pricier than Toyota's model, but it provides more value to driving enthusiasts. The 2026 Honda CR-V Hybrid starts at $35,630. It uses a 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine and electric motors to produce 204 horsepower. The small hybrid SUV achieves 43 miles per gallon in the city and 36 miles per gallon on the highway. I tested the 2026 CR-V Hybrid and found it fun to drive. It has 39.3 cubic feet of cargo space, making its cargo area even roomier than the RAV4's. The CR-V feels refined for a mainstream family SUV and is well-balanced. The greatest noticeable difference between the two Japanese small hybrid SUVs is their respective starting prices. Opting for the CR-V Hybrid over the RAV4 will run you an additional $3,730 before taxes and fees. That price difference gets you a slightly classier family SUV with a bit more cargo space. Toyota's RAV4 comes standard with a 10.5 inch infotainment system screen, which is 1.5 inches longer than the CR-V Hybrid's standard screen. When it comes to value for the money, the Toyota RAV4 s tough to beat because it's significantly more affordable and boasts superior gas mileage. In terms of quality and handling, the CR-V Hybrid has the upper hand. Drivers who find the RAV4 base model too barebones can upgrade to the SE trim for $34,700 and get upgrades like heated front seats and a smart key system. If you can look past the RAV4's interior quality, it's the better small hybrid SUV for the money for drivers in search of value. If you're a driving enthusiast and want a smooth ride and premium materials, the CR-V Hybrid is worth the price difference between the two models. title: Champion Inks Major Partnership With BTS Star V for Global ‘True Champion’ Campaign - Digital Music News
content: Classic sportswear brand Champion has tapped V, from K-pop mega-star group BTS, as the latest brand ambassador for its new global fall campaign, “True Champion.” Known for his cultural influence in music and fashion, V joins a group of celebrities to be featured in the brand’s upcoming campaign, including Sofi Tukker, Bella Sims, Romeo Beckham, Kyle Kuzma, Danna Paola, Megan Kelller, and Jaalen Best. The True Champion campaign launches worldwide on Monday. “True Champion represents a new chapter for Champion and the values that continue to define our brand,” said Stefani Fleurant, Executive Vice President of Marketing, Sports, and Lifestyle at Authentic Brands Group and Champion’s owner. “V’s creative vision, global influence, and genuine connection with his audience make him a natural partner for Champion. Together with an incredible cast of athletes, artists, and creators, this campaign celebrates the many ways people inspire others through who they are and the incredible talent they bring to the world.” “To me, being a ‘True Champion’ isn’t about trying to become someone special,” said V. “Just don’t try too hard to be someone else. I think the more you stay true to yourself, the more confident you’ll become.” The singer called the partnership “a natural fit” and said the values of the campaign resonate personally with him. V, who is no stranger to working with luxury brands, added that being a brand ambassador for Champion is “perfectly in line” with his life since completing his Korean military service. Jamie Salter, Founder and Executive Chairman of Authentic, which acquired Champion from Hanes Brands for $1.2 billion in 2025, ran into V at the World Cup finals at MetLife Stadium last month. The pair posed for a photo on social media that appeared to hint at the upcoming collaboration.

title: Save the Bull Trout and Alliance for the Wild Rockies v. U.S. Department of the Interior and West Side Ditch Company - Mountain States Legal Foundation

For generations, Montana families have relied on the waters of the Upper Clark Fork River to grow hay, care for livestock, and keep their ranches alive. In the high desert of Deer Lodge, where the growing season is short and every drop of water matters, access to irrigation is not a luxury—it is the foundation of a way of life. Today, those families are fighting to protect that way of life. Two radical anti-use organizations have sued a small group of Montana ranching families, claiming that their historic irrigation ditch violates the Endangered Species Act (ESA) because it may affect habitat for the threatened bull trout. Yet they have not identified a single bull trout that the West Side Ditch has actually injured or killed. In fact, the closest bull trout sighting was found more than 30 miles away from the farming operations. Mountain States Legal Foundation has joined in this fight to defend these families because we believe Americans should not lose their property rights, water rights, or livelihoods based on speculation rather than proof. The Endangered Species Act was enacted to prevent actual harm to protected species—not to create a pathway for imposing liability based on uncertain predictions or theoretical impacts. It has never covered any species where there is no real connection between an action and genuine harm. Since 1977, MSLF has fought to protect private property rights, individual liberties, and economic freedom. MSLF is a nonprofit public interest legal foundation. United States District Court for the District of Montana Helena Division The West Side Ditch is more than an irrigation system. It is the lifeline for several small family farms and ranches near Deer Lodge, Montana, providing the water they need to grow hay, irrigate pasture, and feed the livestock that support their livelihoods. Like many of the ranchers who rely on the ditch, the Pauleys aren’t running a massive agricultural operation. They own a modest family ranch, one of several small operations that have spent decades building a future they hoped to pass on to the next generation. “My family is pretty much a first-generation family,” Dalton Pauley explains. “Lots of people are first or second generation. Maybe their parents started in the ’60s, and they worked their whole life just to have something. Now they’re fighting a lawsuit that’s really threatening their livelihoods because these properties just aren’t financially sustainable without our water rights.” For families like the Pauleys, irrigation isn’t about increasing profits. It’s about growing enough hay to feed cattle through Montana’s long winters. Without reliable access to water during the state’s short growing season, many of these ranches simply cannot survive. But today, these families aren’t fighting drought or rising costs. They’re fighting a lawsuit. A coalition of anti-use organizations—Save the Bull Trout and Alliance for the Wild Rockies—claims that the families’ historic irrigation ditch operation violates the Endangered Species Act because it allegedly affects habitat for the threatened bull trout. The Endangered Species Act was enacted to protect threatened and endangered wildlife from actual harm. It prohibits the unauthorized “take” of a protected species, including conduct that kills, injures, or otherwise harms the animal. The plaintiffs argue that by diverting water from the Upper Clark Fork River, the West Side Ditch could affect bull trout habitat by changing streamflows, altering water conditions, making fish passage more difficult, or creating a risk that trout could enter the irrigation ditch. No one has identified a single bull trout that the West Side Ditch has actually injured or killed. Instead, the lawsuit asks the court to hold these families liable based on the possibility that their lawful irrigation practices could indirectly affect the fish or its habitat. Mountain States Legal Foundation exists to defend Americans whose rights are threatened by government overreach and abusive litigation. The families who rely on the West Side Ditch are exactly the people MSLF was created to protect. The Endangered Species Act requires evidence—not speculation. It was written to address actual harm, not hold people liable for what might happen. MSLF is asking the court to reject an attempt to hold the West Side Ditch Company and the Pauley family responsible for harm they did not cause and allow the families to use their irrigation systems as they have for decades. The stakes extend far beyond one irrigation ditch in Montana. If speculation alone is enough to create liability, the same theory could threaten farmers, ranchers, property owners, energy producers, miners, timber workers, and communities across the country that depend on responsible use of natural resources. Rozanne Goglia Whipple, born June 14, 1946, passed away peacefully on Sunday, August 9, 2026, surrounded by those she loved most. A devoted wife, mother, grandmother, servant of God, and friend to many, Rozanne lived a life marked by faith, compassion, and a steadfast commitment to serving others. Rozanne was married to the love of her life, Oliver Cleveland Whipple, in January 1969. Together they shared more than five decades of marriage, building a loving home grounded in faith, family, and service. She was the beloved mother of Ellen Delbridge and her husband, Larry, and Oliver Christian Whipple and his wife, Ronda. She was a proud and loving grandmother to Avery Paige Whipple, Mary Elizabeth Guthrie, Oliver Coleman Whipple, John Cleveland Guthrie, and Claire Elizabeth Whipple. Her grandchildren were among her greatest joys, and she cherished each of them deeply. Rozanne was preceded in death by her parents, Mario and Juanita Goglia, and her only sibling, David Goglia. After dedicating many years to her family as a homemaker, Rozanne discovered her calling in local missions and service to those in need. Through Vidalia Presbyterian Church, she faithfully ministered to members of her community, offering kindness, support, and practical help to countless individuals and families. Her passion for serving others later led her to work with the Department of Family and Children Services, where she continued to make a meaningful difference in the lives of those she served. A woman of deep and abiding faith, Rozanne served as an Elder at Vidalia Presbyterian Church, where she oversaw Christian Education and was a devoted Sunday school teacher. She loved sharing God's Word and helping others grow in their faith. Later in life, God called Rozanne back to the Catholic Church. There she continued her lifelong commitment to faith and fellowship, becoming a familiar and beloved presence in her parish community. An avid reader, teacher, and friend, she shared her warmth, wisdom, and encouragement with fellow parishioners, priests, and all who knew her. Rozanne will be remembered for her gentle spirit, generous heart, unwavering faith, and boundless love for her family. She had a gift for making others feel welcome, valued, and loved. Her life was a testament to Christian service, and her legacy will live on in the many lives she touched. While her family mourns her passing, they take comfort in knowing she is at peace in the presence of her Lord and reunited with those who have gone before her. “Well done, good and faithful servant.” She will be deeply missed, forever loved, and always remembered. A memorial graveside service will be held on Saturday afternoon, August 15th, 2026, at 1:00 at Lakeview Memorial Gardens with Father Ben Dallas officiating. title: SBIR Phase III Bid Protests- What Strategi Consulting v. U.S. Means for Government Contractors - The National Law Review
content: The National Law Review uses cookies to track usage trends and patterns to better understand and improve our website. By using this website and/or clicking on any link on the website, you confirm your consent to the NLR’s placing and usage of cookies. In Strategi Consulting, LLC v. United States, the U.S. Court of Federal Claims recently held that a prior Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) Phase II awardee can bring a bid protest when an agency declines to award it Phase III work and instead routes that work to other contractors through existing task orders — even without a formal solicitation. The court denied the government’s motion to dismiss, confirming that (1) informal “insourcing” and de facto follow-on work can count as a “procurement,” (2) the Federal Acquisition Streamlining Act (FASA) Task Order Bar does not block claims that are only tangentially related to task orders, and (3) SBIR’s Phase III preference statute supports injunctive and declaratory relief in a bid protest. Strategi Consulting held a Phase II SBIR contract with Space Systems Command to build Voltron, a Tactical Surveillance, Reconnaissance, and Tracking (TacSRT) platform for the Air Force and Space Force. The contract closed in November 2025 with all deliverables accepted, and Voltron earned an Authorization-to-Operate equivalent certification. Strategi alleged that, rather than award it a Phase III contract, the Air Force Research Lab funneled continuation work to Dragon Army, a “pooled, badge-less, multi-contractor” internal organization that used existing task orders with four private contractors to build Vigil — a platform Strategi claims replicates Voltron’s architecture and backlog. Strategi also alleged the agency demanded Strategi’s codebase and that a government program lead made statements reflecting bias against the company. The government moved to dismiss, arguing there was no “procurement” for the court to review; the claim was barred by FASA’s Task Order Bar; and Strategi’s requested relief was not redressable in a bid protest. The court reaffirmed that “procurement” under 28 U.S.C. § 1491(b)(1) is interpreted broadly — it covers the entire process of determining a need for property or services, not just formal solicitations. Citing Distributed Solutions, Diaz, and Santa Barbara Applied Research, the court held that an agency’s decision to develop functionally equivalent software through existing contractors, after declining a Phase II contractor’s Phase III proposal, is “acquisition by another name” and falls within the court’s bid protest jurisdiction. The court distinguished ASTi v. United States, where the disputed software had been developed decades earlier with no active solicitation; here, the agency had recently funded the technology, declined a live Phase III proposal, and continued near-identical development through contractors. The FASA Task Order Bar (41 U.S.C. § 4106(f)) generally prohibits protests at the court regarding the “issuance or proposed issuance” of a task order. The court held that Strategi’s claim survives because it targets the agency’s alleged violation of the SBIR Phase III preference — the task orders are merely the vehicle, not the subject, of the protest. The court also noted FASA’s increased-scope exception would independently apply if the disputed work exceeded what the task orders actually covered. The government argued that Strategi’s claims were not redressable because courts generally cannot order an agency to buy a specific product. The court rejected that framing: Strategi sought a ruling that the agency’s conduct was arbitrary and an injunction against assigning the disputed work to other contractors — relief expressly authorized under 28 U.S.C. § 1491(b)(2). Strategi Consulting v. United States gives SBIR Phase II awardees a real avenue to challenge agencies that quietly move follow-on work to other contractors or internal teams instead of honoring the Phase III preference. Contractors facing a similar pattern — proposal submitted, no formal response, then substantially similar work appearing elsewhere — should document the timeline carefully and consult experienced protest counsel promptly. title: Champion Names V of BTS as the Face of “True Champion” - dscene magazine
content: Champion names V of BTS as the face of its new “True Champion” campaign, marking the start of a global partnership with the South Korean singer and songwriter. The FW26 project places V at the center of Champion’s latest chapter, with a focus on individuality, creative identity and the influence that artists and athletes bring to contemporary culture. V, whose given name is Kim Taehyung, brings an established presence in music and fashion to the partnership. As a member of BTS, he has built an international following while developing a distinct visual identity through solo projects, performances and personal style. His first solo album, Layover, arrived in 2023, drawing from jazz and R&B influences with a more intimate musical direction. That interest carries into the Champion campaign imagery. V appears in a series of relaxed looks that draw from varsity, collegiate and athletic dressing. Oversized jackets, quarter zip tops, sweatpants, rugby inspired pieces and retro sneakers shape the wardrobe, creating a casual visual language that fits closely with the way he approaches off duty style. V has described choosing his clothes according to what feels right in the moment, often combining different influences without following a fixed formula. Casual pieces form an important part of that approach, especially simple T-shirts and comfortable silhouettes. Among the pieces featured, V singles out a gray long sleeve shirt with a red Champion logo as a personal favorite. The red detail gives the otherwise simple piece a stronger visual point, matching his preference for adding touches of red to his outfits. Champion uses V’s involvement to introduce “True Champion” as a campaign centered on people shaping culture through their own perspectives. The partnership connects the brand’s athletic identity with V’s influence in music, fashion and visual culture, giving the campaign a global lead figure with a clear personal point of view. The wider FW26 campaign also includes Romeo Beckham, SOFI TUKKER, Kyle Kuzma, Danna Paola, Megan Keller, Bella Sims and Jaalen Best. Their involvement extends the project into sports, music and entertainment, while V leads the first visual chapter of “True Champion.” Jana Kostic is an Editor at DSCENE Publishing, holding a Master’s degree in Electrical and Computer Engineering from Belgrade. title: Client Alert: Subchapter V Surge: What Florida Trade Creditors and Lenders Need to Know About the New Small Business Bankruptcy Landscape - JD Supra
content:
Florida lenders and trade creditors are confronting a rapidly shifting landscape in small business insolvency. In the first quarter of 2026 alone, small business elections under Subchapter V of Chapter 11 surged 67 percent year over year, according to Epiq AACER data. This is not a blip. It is a sustained, accelerating trend that fundamentally alters how creditors interact with financially distressed borrowers and the timeline within which they must act to protect their recoveries. For regional banks, credit unions, fintechs, and trade creditors serving Florida's small business economy, understanding Subchapter V is no longer optional. It is an operational imperative. According to Epiq AACER data, Subchapter V elections for small businesses totaled 833 in the first quarter of 2026, compared with just 499 in the same period of 2025. Total commercial Chapter 11 filings rose 37 percent, from 1,764 to 2,422, while overall commercial bankruptcies climbed 14 percent to 8,436. Critically, this distress is not concentrated in a single industry. The increase in Subchapter V filings is broad and sector spanning, with elevated risk in retail, food service, transportation, and construction. Epiq AACER has flagged "large pockets of concentrated increases within creditor portfolios," underscoring the need for proactive receivables monitoring across diverse lending and credit exposures. Perhaps the most significant departure is the elimination of the unsecured creditors' committee unless specific "cause" exists to appoint one. Under traditional Chapter 11, a committee is appointed as a matter of course, providing a collective voice and investigative capacity funded by the estate. In Subchapter V, no committee is formed unless the court orders one "for cause" under 11 U.S.C. § 1181(b), an exceedingly rare occurrence. This removes a critical institutional check on debtor conduct and places the burden of vigilance squarely on individual creditors. Subchapter V eliminates the disclosure statement requirement, reducing debtor cost and time but correspondingly reducing the information available to creditors. Although the Subchapter V debtor must include background and financial details in its plan, the level of information required in a traditional Chapter 11 disclosure statement is typically not presented. Additionally, only the debtor may file a plan of reorganization—no competing creditor plans are permitted—and that plan must be filed within 90 days of the order for relief unless extended for cause under 11 U.S.C. § 1189. Creditor participation in plan approval is limited to objections, negotiations, and voting and input. The absolute priority rule does not apply. Equity holders may retain ownership even if unsecured creditors are not paid in full, so long as the debtor commits projected disposable income over the plan's life. Most consequentially, a plan can be confirmed non-consensually (i.e., "crammed down") even if no class of creditors votes to accept it and over creditor objections, provided the court finds it "fair and equitable" under 11 U.S.C. § 1191(b). A Subchapter V trustee is appointed in every case, but the trustee's primary role is to facilitate consensus, not to advocate for creditors. A creditor's ability to object to confirmation may be its only practical means of protecting its interests in a Subchapter V case. The Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act of 2026 (S. 3977), introduced March 3, 2026, would permanently raise the Subchapter V debt eligibility threshold to $7.5 million, up from the current inflation-adjusted threshold of approximately $3.42 million, which reverted down after the pandemic-era temporary cap expired on June 21, 2024. On August 3, 2026, the bill unanimously passed in the Senate and will next be considered by the House. A companion bill in the House advanced out of the House Judiciary Committee, indicating previous initial bipartisan approval of raising the debt cap. If enacted, the $7.5 million threshold would substantially expand the pool of borrowers eligible for the faster, committee-free Subchapter V process. Action: Identify borrowers in the $3.42 million–$7.5million debt range who would become newly eligible. Despite the compressed timeline and reduced creditor protections, Subchapter V produces materially better reorganization outcomes than its predecessors. According to 2024 data from the American Bankruptcy Institute's Subchapter V Task Force, approximately 50 percent of Subchapter V cases that reach disposition result in a confirmed reorganization plan. By comparison, traditional small business Chapter 11 cases confirmed at a rate of roughly 23 to 25 percent before Subchapter V's enactment. For creditors, the higher confirmation rate means reorganization plans are more likely to be imposed, making early engagement critical. But the faster timeline and improved debtor viability also mean that creditors who engage strategically may recover more than they would from the protracted and often unsuccessful traditional process. Given the accelerated timelines, reduced institutional safeguards, and the debtor's enhanced leverage under Subchapter V, creditors must be proactive. The following strategies are essential: ✓  Flag all borrowers in sectors with elevated Sub V filings (retail, food service, transportation, construction) ✓  Identify portfolio exposures in the $3.42 million-$7.5 million range (newly eligible if threshold bill passes) ✓  Establish internal protocols for 90-day plan timeline response ✓  Pre-identify counsel and Rule 2004 discovery request templates for rapid deployment ✓  Calendar adequate protection and cash collateral motions within first 14 days of any filing The Subchapter V surge is not a temporary phenomenon. It reflects structural economic pressures that show no sign of abating, legislative momentum toward expanding eligibility, and a process that, by design, favors speed and debtor rehabilitation over creditor deliberation. Florida lenders and trade creditors who invest now in understanding the Subchapter V framework, building internal monitoring capabilities, and developing rapid response protocols will be far better positioned to protect their interests when—not if—a borrower in their portfolio elects this path. DISCLAIMER: Because of the generality of this update, the information provided herein may not be applicable in all situations and should not be acted upon without specific legal advice based on particular situations.

For Dr. Laposata, what we have is a two and a half page letter to attorney Reddington outlining her thoughts, but it doesn't say what her opinions are based on. (03:43:11)It doesn't say which materials she's reviewed and what she's relying on. So I would suggest that it's an insufficient report. And again, with the delayed disclosure... For example, she talks about Jefferson fracture causing the injuries. Well, if we had this information previously and knew this is what they were going to argue, we could have obtained our own expert to talk about the mechanism of injury and Jefferson fractures and all of those things. But we weren't told until a week before trial that she would even potentially be a witness. And then we get this report on July 26th that's a two and a half page letter. But didn't we have multiple trauma surgeons, neurosurgeons who've testified, who treated her? Couldn't someone just ask, is that consistent with... And that's pretty much from looking at Dr. Laposata's note. I'm not sure I would allow in opinions regarding whether or not it's a serious suicide or not, but she does indicate it's consistent with landing on an individual's head. Well, your Honor, we had a trauma surgeon from the South Shore Hospital testify who said that the injuries that Ms. Clancy sustained were a level one and she had to be transported to another hospital where doctors who were trained in those injuries could operate on her. So we didn't think that she would have the knowledge and the training and experience to testify about the nature of those injuries and how they occur. The trauma surgeon from Brigham and Women's Hospital is with the military and is overseas in the Middle East and so was unavailable. But had we known that this was going to be an issue and they were going to allege this particular type of fracture, we would have endeavored to get another expert in replace of the doctor who treated her at Brigham and Women's. But we didn't know that this would even be an issue until a week before trial. (03:45:10)And again, this letter is dated July 26th and it doesn't tell us which records, which reports or what medical journals or training or anything that these opinions are based on. Well, that could be done by voir dire. I mean, the Commonwealth has at least inferred through their case that this was not a serious suicide attempt. Right? I mean, and there's questions about whether or not somebody's hanging outside the window or not. And so why wasn't this an issue that the Commonwealth could have anticipated would come up? The position of the Commonwealth isn't that it wasn't a serious suicide attempt. It's that the methods that were chosen were insufficient to achieve the goal. And the reasons for that we would argue in our closing, I don't think we have to disclose that theory at this point, but we've never said it wasn't a serious suicide attempt. We've never said it was a fake suicide attempt. What we've endeavored to develop from the testimony is that the methods that were chosen were methods that would be unsuccessful, but we're not saying it wasn't a serious attempt. And I think the reasons for that will become clearer when the doctors give their testimony. But it's our position that she was attempting to kill herself that night. And there are various reasons and factors where she was unsuccessful in killing herself, but successful in killing her children. But there's been all kinds of testimony regarding, it seems to be a dispute of whether or not she's hanging from the window sill or goes out head first. There's some testimony that's been raised even with the blood experts and things that she may have been hanging from the window sill. Dr. Laposata, it seems what they're seeking in is those injuries are consistent with somebody who lands on their head. So would the court allow us to call a witness who's not on our witness list to rebut that evidence? And this is why I didn't make a decision on this earlier because I have to see how the case develops. And this issue of how this injury occurs is certainly, it's either been specifically and explicitly raised or inferred in multiple questions, even to the length of, to the part of the cuts and things like that. It's been over and over and over. So if the Commonwealth seeks to get somebody to rebut that, I would strongly consider that. In regards to Dr. Laposata's opinion, we may need a voir dire in regards to, but I wouldn't imagine the voir dire would take that long. It would be, did you view the x-rays? I mean, that kind of an injury is probably pretty clear on the x-rays or the MRIs. If we could get a list from defense counsel on what she's basing her opinion on so we can have our witness review the same material. I can tell you right now, it's just simple. It's just the South Shore Hospital medical records, Brigham and Women's medical records that have already been discussed with the jury. Why don't we do this just so it's clear because when a witness is on the stand, it's much easier to have something in writing to say, "Is this what you relied on?" So if you could get from Dr. Laposata what she is relying upon to form that opinion. Like I said, I'm inclined to allow that opinion. And I would allow then the Commonwealth to present a rebuttal witness if they seek to. But also the third expert, what we have here is a letter dated August 4th. That's a page and a half that's not even signed by, I believe it's Dr- Yeah. I'm more concerned with that is whether or not the opinion is admissible. The opinion as I see it is he's reviewed the medical records and it's his opinion. These are injuries that commonly observed in the quote serious suicide attempts. Their doctors waxed eloquently about suicide and whether or not it's- But I'm just concerned that how are we going to parse out what he looked at? A hundred other cases and then we go through into all of those. So I'm going to have to take a look. That's what I'm going to take under advisement for sure. That doesn't mean he may have other opinions I'm going to have to look at. I think he talked about some of his observations as an emergency room doctor, I think, didn't he? Yeah. I'm more reluctant to allow in that individual's opinion that this was a suicide attempt. So their South Shore doctors are able to talk about superficial, superficial as we've heard for a week now. But his opinion that it's consistent with what he's observed in his emergency room treatment is not admissible. What I'm saying is that he can't necessarily give the opinion, I've looked at this. It's my opinion, this was a suicide attempt. But he could certainly testify. I've looked at the cuts. These are the phrase superficial. I think that's been mixed up in this whole thing too. That seems to be more of a medical term as opposed to- Well, no. They basically beat it to death with not being a medical term until we were able to show that in fact it was deep 3.5 and 2. Okay. Yeah. I mean, if you want to call this doctor, he's going to say that's a significant cut. That's different than saying, looking at that, I find that this is a suicide attempt. Just like there's never been an opinion here that this was not a suicide attempt. That's probably something that the jury- Well, that's going to probably be for the jury to determine. But I would allow going into the characteristics that have already been testified to. We need a further voir dire on that doctor as well. But I think he lists in there what he reviewed. All right. Anything else in regards to those three witnesses? So I'm going to take this under advisement, but just for... What I'm inclined to do is I'm going to take a look at Dr. Conti's report and compare it to some of the other reports. I'm inclined to let Dr. Laposata testify that the injuries are consistent with basically a fall on the head. And the last doctor, I've got to take a look at his language, but I would not be allowing in his opinion that this is a suicide attempt. But he may testify as to all the other observations that he took from those records. All right. Understood. Just note my objection for what it's worth. All right. And so I'll note the Commonwealth's objection. I'll note the defendant's objection. And like I said, I'll take it under advisement and everybody can renew those objections Again. As it relates to Conti, once you make your decision, you let me know. I can certainly reach out to him and have him delete this standard as to standard of care and just reference the actual treatment and prescriptions that she received. All Right. So I'll take a look at this... I'll have this tomorrow morning for everybody when you come in. Just in case there's a problem. Dr. Laposata has been working with a gentleman by the name of Mr. Drake, Drake Laboratories that is putting together an auto computer animated display of coming out the window, the injuries to the neck, showing the vertebrae and that type of thing, which is all based upon evidence that's already in evidence here. So I haven't got it yet. It's not done yet. So I don't want to not say anything about it now because they'll be objecting to it tomorrow, I'm sure. Or whenever it's ready. I assume we'll have to take a look at that and give the Commonwealth the opportunity to view it and hear the arguments in regards. It may be something nobody has objected to or maybe. I don't know. All right? Well, it goes back to the whole position that we have the right to, if we want to obtain another expert- ... and then that expert could review that material and use it to form his opinion. This is different than the 3D diagram of the house that the Commonwealth gave. The defense was on notice that that was becoming the basis of it, the measurements, what the house looked like itself. And so that was turned over. This is completely different. And I just note that, as I said, the medical records that the government has talks about Jefferson Fracture. You might remember two weeks ago or two and a half weeks ago when they first raised their objection, I told you that I can't know what they're going to argue until they argue it. So I didn't know whether or not they were going to say that it's a fake suicide or that she didn't jump out the window. I had to wait to see what their opening was. Now I know I have to rebut it. We were almost out of here till you mentioned that BD thing. So why don't we do this? We'll wait on that. All right. I'm not committing one way or the other in regards to that. We'll see. So maybe the testimony with the 3D, the testimony without the 3D. We'll just see where we go. All right. All right. So thanks everybody for buckling down and going through that so we could resolve that as best we can. I appreciate that. So we'll be in recess on this matter till tomorrow morning at 9:00 o'clock. title: The Rezvani Beast X Is a Last Gasp for GM’s 6.2-Liter V-8 - Car and Driver
content:
The new Corvette-based hypercar from Rezvani produces 1560 horsepower and looks more like a jet fighter than a sports car. The idea of someone building a Corvette with four-digit horsepower numbers just isn’t that mind-blowing, at least not in 2026. Hell, if you’ve got the coin, Chevy will sell you two production versions of the Corvette with north of 1000 ponies, and those come with a factory-backed warranty. But a Vette with jet-fighter looks, a roof scoop, and 1560 horsepower? That’s not something you see every day. Enter the Rezvani Beast X. Remember the last Rezvani Beast? This one is sort of like that, though it’s got quite a bit more X Factor. In real terms, that means the team of engineers over at Rezvani managed to squeeze 1560 horsepower out of what we believe is the Corvette E-Ray’s hybrid-assisted 6.2-liter V-8. They did that by slapping a pair of turbochargers onto the combustion end of the E-Ray’s powertrain equation. Power is sent to all four wheels, and according to Rezvani, that mega power figure means the Beast X can launch from zero to 60 mph in 1.9 seconds. The reimagined Corvette’s body is built entirely from carbon fiber—allowing it to shed some weight compared with the standard Corvette. According to Rezvani, the bodywork isn’t just for looks; the automaker reportedly designed every surface to optimize airflow and stability at high speeds. A set of magnesium wheels also helps with the Beast X’s diet, reducing unsprung mass by a substantial seven pounds per wheel, Rezvani claims. The changes should improve acceleration, help the car slow down more quickly, and result in sharper steering response. Like with every other car Rezvani decides to rework, production of the Beast X will be kept extremely limited. The automaker is taking $1500 refundable deposits to allocate a production slot, though you may have to move quickly if you want one, considering that Rezvani will only build five examples of the Beast X. By hounding his college professors at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, he was able to travel Wisconsin seeking out stories in the auto world before landing his dream job at Car and Driver. title: Real Salt Lake Hosts 2026 Leagues Cup Tuesday in Must-Win Match V FC Juárez - Real Salt Lake
content: RSL Remains in Utah for Must-Win Leagues Cup Phase One Finale; Tuesday Match Third of Five Home Games from August 4-19, Including Three Liga MX Contests; Tickets for All Home Events Remain Available via www.RSL.com/Tickets SANDY, Utah (Monday, August 10, 2026) – This week, Real Salt Lake (8W-6L-3T, 27 points, 5th West MLS / 9th Shield) remains home for the third of at least three 2026 Leagues Cup home matches with Tuesday’s 7:30p MT kickoff against emerging Liga MX side FC Juárez. This week’s must-win match marks the third of five RSL home games in a 15-day span on the Wasatch Front, with a trio of Leagues Cup contests and two MLS regular-season matches through August 19. Following Saturday’s dominant 4-0 win against Liga MX upstart Atlante CF – one which snapped a five-game winless run across multiple competitions – RSL now owns a 9-1-1 (W-L-T) mark on Utah soil in 2026, outscoring visitors 27-10, with the lone setback coming on April 22 in an 0-2 loss to Inter Miami CF. Since June 1, 2025, RSL is 17-4-3 (W-L-T) at home, while the weekend’s victory improved RSL to 7-6-6 all-time against Mexican visitors in the last 22 seasons, with a 19-10-8 mark on the Wasatch Front against all international opponents. Tuesday’s RSL Leagues Cup contest on Apple TV features Mark Rogondino and Heath Pearce on the primary English-language call, with Carlos Ramirez and Max Cordaro providing the Spanish-language analysis. Simultaneously, the KSL Radio team of David James and Jay Nolly return to the mic, with Nelson Moran – now in his 22nd RSL season as RSL’s Spanish radio voice – conducting the Spanish call on KBMG Latino 106.3 FM. GAME NOTES for Tuesday’s RSL v FC Juarez Match Available Online The Adobe PDF version of the 2026 RSL Game Guide in advance of Tuesday’s Leagues Cup contest between Real Salt Lake and FC Juárez can be found HERE. Media members looking to receive the document as an attachment or have further questions are asked to please contact RSL Communications via email at RSLcommunications@RSL.com. With heavy rotation to the weekend lineup due to schedule congestion, RSL Head Coach Pablo Mastroeni made six changes to the starting XI, with rookie FW Sergi Solans, playmaker Diego Luna and Utah native Zach Booth joining Noel Caliskan and DeAndre Yedlin in the selection after brief respites on Tuesday. In the game’s 16th minute, Solans found the back of the net for his 10th goal of the season (seven in MLS, two vs. Burnley), the RSL Golden Boot leader opening his Leagues Cup account on the first of two assists by Luna on the night. When scoring first during the Mastroeni era, RSL is now 55-11-21 (W-L-T) since August, 2021, while taking a 1-0 lead. Just five minutes into the second half, RSL blew the game open with a pair of goals in short succession, as Eden, Utah native Booth – making just his sixth start of the season – scored his first-ever home goal (and second overall) with a blistering left-footed shot from 18 yards out. Shortly thereafter, Lukas Engel deftly redirected a Morgan Guilavogui pass off a Luna free kick, the Danish defender scoring his second goal in the last five matches – after being shut out in his first 49 career MLS appearances. Wrapping up RSL’s first four-goal win in more than two years was veteran RSL midfielder Pablo Ruiz, who followed up Tuesday’s equalizer – his first goal since a midfield bombazo in June, 2023, at D.C. United, a span of just 35 games played across 1,444 days due to two severe knee injuries for the metronomic, deep-lying playmaker – with a hard, left-footed shot far post after picking the Atlante player’s pocket for his second goal of the week. Led by “Iron Man” goalkeeper and Captain Rafael Cabral – who has played every minute of all 60 matches since arriving at RSL in January, 2025 – RSL earned its third clean sheet of the season with the blanking of Atlante, all three shutouts coming at home. First-year Colombian centerback Juan Jose Arias made his second consecutive start in impressive fashion, while Engel, Yedlin, Caliskan and holding mid Stijn Spierings – making his 13th start in 14 matches – defused numerous opposing attacks. Tuesday’s match against Juarez is the sixth amidst a critical stretch of 11 games in 44 days for RSL across both MLS and Leagues Cup contests, a run that began with late July road losses at LAFC and Portland. While the St. Louis draw snapped a two-game losing streak in RSL’s post-World Cup slate following losses at LAFC on July 22 and at Portland on July 25, the Club is forced to carry an active seven-game winless streak away from home into its next road match, August 22 at Orlando. Despite the recent spate of winless matches, RSL remains in fifth place in a tightly-packed MLS Western Conference with 17 games remaining in its 22nd all-time MLS season, with Tuesday’s match four weeks removed from a 4-1 home exhibition win over English Championship side Burnley FC - the first of at least four international clubs to arrive on the Wasatch Front during a 30-day midsummer span. Real Salt Lake Head Coach Pablo Mastroeni has now managed the Club in 204 matches across all competitions, registering 84 wins, 72 losses and 48 draws in MLS, Audi MLS Cup Playoffs, Leagues Cup, Open Cup, Concacaf Champions Cup and international friendly contests since late August, 2021. The former U.S. Men’s National Team World Cup standout (2002, 2006), MLS Cup Champion (2010) as a player, and former Colorado Rapids manager (2014-16) has averaged 1.60 points per game with RSL in his 202 matches at the helm. Only Cup-winning former manager Jason Kreis (2007-13) – now the Club’s President of Soccer – boasts more games, more wins and a higher PPG average than Mastroeni in RSL’s 22 seasons. During the Mastroeni era, resilience, grit and determination have served as trademarks for RSL, with the Club suffering back-to-back losses on just 20 occasions in those 204 games. Last Saturday at St. Louis marked the latest opportunity for the Claret-and-Cobalt to display its “xDAWG” mentality as it earned the result at Energizer Park, previously winning 35 and drawing 17 times in “bounce-back” games following a loss in Mastroeni’s five-plus seasons in Utah. Competing on the Wasatch Front, the Atlante CF win Saturday boosts RSL’s all-time record against Mexican visitors to an 7W-6L-6T on the Wasatch Front, where RSL has now outscored the Liga MX sides 26-25 over the years on their collective visits. A must-win Phase One finale remains for RSL against FC Juárez, with RSL needing to accrue seven points, and likely requiring a very heavy goal differential in order to advance to the Quarterfinals as one of four MLS sides to emerge from the 18 currently in the competition. Real Salt Lake entered the tourney ranked as the 30th overall side out of 36 participants based on its 2025 performance and standings results, with RSL fifth of the six teams in the West 1 pod, which also includes MLS sides Vancouver and Minnesota, in addition to RSL’s three Liga MX opponents. Further information on each match can be found at www.RSL.com or www.LeaguesCup.com. FC JUÁREZ also makes its maiden visit to Utah as part of the 2026 Leagues Cup, RSL hosting another first-time opponent. Juarez was founded as a second-division side in 2015, ascending to Liga MX in 2019 as a replacement for Lobos BUAP. Former RSL Academy, Real Monarchs and RSL forward and Park City, Utah native Sebastian “Bofo” Saucedo played 17 games for FC Juarez from 2023-25, scoring one goal. Now in its fourth edition, Leagues Cup 2026 will once again award three spots in the 2027 CONCACAF Champions Cup, where the winner will represent the region at FIFA international club competitions, with the Leagues Cup 2026 champion earning a direct berth to the Round of 16. A year ago, RSL drew with both Club América and Atlético San Luis at home before winning against Queretaro, splitting the shootout tiebreakers in the first two matches. RSL Captain and GK Rafa Cabral enjoyed perhaps his signature moment in the dramatic penalty-kick session against Las Aguilas, denying several attempts from the spot after América scored deep into second-half stoppage time to force the draw. Three days later against Atlético San Luis, RSL saw late dramatics from former MF Braian Ojeda force the tiebreaker, the Claret-and-Cobalt conceding the extra point in the group standings against 2026 newcomer Juan Manuel Sanabria’s former side. In last year’s group stage finale, RSL defeated Queretaro by a narrow 1-0 scoreline in a match dominated by RSL, which conceded just a lone shot on goal over the 90 minutes, Ojeda again providing the match-winner. Running from August 4 through September 6, Leagues Cup 2026 will feature 36 clubs – all 18 LIGA MX teams and 18 qualified MLS clubs. All 54 matches during Phase One along with the Quarterfinals will deliver LIGA MX vs. MLS matchups and feature defending Leagues Cup champion Seattle Sounders, top-rated LIGA MX Club Toluca, 2025 MLS Cup Champion Inter Miami, as well as 2025 Concacaf Champions Cup winner Cruz Azul and runner-up Vancouver Whitecaps. title: V of BTS Is a ‘True Champion’ as the New Ambassador for This Iconic Fashion Brand - Billboard
content:
He's representing the company's "winning spirit" alongside Romeo Beckham, Sofi Tukker and more. V‘s been a champion on the charts as a member of BTS, and now, he’s a champion of one fashion brand’s latest campaign. As announced on Monday (Aug. 10), the K-pop superstar is now the leading face of “True Champion” by Champion, representing the sporty clothing label globally alongside Romeo Beckham, Danna Paola, Kyle Kuzma, Sofi Tukker, Megan Keller, Bella Sims and Jaalen Best. In photos shared by the company on Instagram, V gazes into the camera while modeling a dark blue hoodie. “A history of wins that began with a winning spirit — and the determination to keep showing up,” reads a description of the campaign on Champion’s website. “But unspoken greatness is what sets true champions apart from the rest. It is an energy that needs no audience or explanation.” In a statement, Stefani Fleurant — executive VP of marketing, sport and lifestyle at Authentic Brands Group, which acquired Champion in 2024 — praised V’s “creative vision, global influence and genuine connection with his audience,” explaining that those traits making him a “natural partner” for the brand. “This campaign celebrates the many ways people inspire others through who they are and the incredible talent they bring to the world.” The South Korean performer is no stranger to fashion partnerships, having previously served as a global ambassador for brands such as Cartier and Celine. In May, V and his BTS bandmates collectively teamed up with Nike for a customizable collection celebrating their ongoing ARIRANG World Tour. The boy band — which has notched seven No. 1s on the Billboard Hot 100 to date — just completed two nights at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Mass. The septet’s next two shows will take place back to back starting Monday night in Baltimore, with the ARIRANG trek set to complete its North American leg in early September. BTS’ most recent album, ARIRANG, spent three weeks atop the Billboard 200. See the announcement of V’s partnership with Champion below and shop the pieces online at Champion and Target.com. title: Forty Under 40: Sarah V. Livengood - Talk Business & Politics
content: by Talk Business & Politics staff (staff2@talkbusiness.net)  8 hours ago 101 views Sarah Livengood was in graduate school when she started volunteering at the Yvonne Richardson Community Center in Fayetteville. This led to a full-time job as a program coordinator at the city-owned center in 2016. She was responsible for its youth programs that received multiple Program of the Year Awards from the Arkansas Recreation and Parks Association. “That’s really what launched me back into service to the community,” she said. “And I haven’t looked back since then.” The Pfafftown, N.C., native moved to Northwest Arkansas in 2012 to attend the University of Arkansas. She earned master’s degrees in anthropology from the UA and Georgia State University. Livengood joined nonprofit Arkansas Community Foundation in September after her first child was born. She started in her existing role for the Fayetteville affiliate, which serves Washington County. “I needed something that had a good balance for what my life looks like now compared to when I started in the nonprofit/community sector, but also something that pulled together all of the different arenas that I have been sitting in from health, youth development, and all of that based in relationships, community partnerships, networking,” she said. “And that’s what this job really is.” She builds relationships with nonprofits, cities, universities, and the philanthropic organizations that want to support them. She works with the foundation’s board members on grants and scholarships. She’s increased grant applicant volumes by 354% and led a rise in scholarship applications across multiple funds, with several programs doubling or tripling applicant pools year over year. Livengood supports Girl Scouts Diamonds of Arkansas, Oklahoma and Texas, for which she was program director. She enjoys crafting, gardening and reading. title: Thelma V. Davis - WGEL Radio
content: Thelma V. Davis, beloved mother, grandmother, and great-grandmother, passed away peacefully on August 7th, 2026. She was 74 years old. Born in Tacloban City, Philippines, on May 5th, 1952, Thelma was the daughter of Natividad and Victor Varona. She was one of five children and is preceded in death by her brothers Bobby and Henry. She is survived by her brother Bundoy and sister Ninette, both of Manila, Philippines. On March 31, 1973, Thelma married Charles Raymond Davis, Sr., with whom she shared a loving marriage until his passing in 2010. Together, they raised two children: Charles “Charlie” R. Davis, Jr., of Greenville, and Tina Gladue (Matthew) of Stafford, Virginia. She was a proud grandmother to Easton Gladue (Camille), serving in the U.S. Army at Fort Bragg, NC, and Shawn Gladue (Savannah), serving in the U.S. Space Force at Shriever Base, CO. She also leaves behind one great-grandchild, Brinley Grace Gladue, Thelma’s life was marked by resilience, generosity, and faith. Raised in poverty and forced to leave school in the third grade, she devoted herself to helping others- funding the education of nieces and nephews, supporting charities for the hungry and orphaned, and giving freely to family, friends, and neighbors. A devout Catholic, she was a faithful member of St. Lawrence Catholic Church, where she often led the rosary in prayer for others. In her final years, Thelma was lovingly cared for by her son Charlie, who selflessly supported her through her decline. Even after she was placed in a nursing home, Charlie visited her twice daily- feeding her, praying with her, and ensuring she was never alone. His devotion was a living reflection of the love Thelma gave throughout her life. In accordance with her wishes, Thelma will be cremated, and her ashes laid to rest with her beloved husband, Charles. Her children have chosen to grieve privately and will hold a celebration of her life at a later date. Her legacy is one of selfless love, and the deep affection she inspired in her family and community is a reflection of the grace she gave so freely. The family has entrusted Assalley Funeral Home in Greenville with the ceremonies. Please visit [www.assalleyfuneralhomes.com](http://www.assalleyfuneralhomes.com) to share memories or offer condolences to the family.

title: Ultrarunner and LeLa V founder Erika Reyes releases debut memoir on resilience and self-belief - ABC7 WWSB
content: SARASOTA, Fla. (WWSB) - Ultrarunner, entrepreneur, and LeLa V founder Erika Reyes has released her debut memoir, Breaking the Cycle: How I Ran My Way to a New Beginning Through Ultrarunning, Resilience, and Self-Belief. The book centers on overcoming adversity, rediscovering purpose, and the role of incremental progress in personal transformation. Reyes addresses several themes throughout the book, including finding clarity through movement, shifting away from physical activity as punishment or restriction, and building resilience through early life instability. She also writes about finding the courage to take action when feeling stuck and developing self-belief through small, consistent habits. Reyes said the book is dedicated in part to young adults, drawing on her own experience with diagnosed depression. “Part of the reason I dedicate my book to young adults is that I suffered from diagnosed depression,” Reyes said. “This took a significant emotional toll and I lacked the self-belief regarding my ability to play any sports. Once I passed this phase of my life, a big weight lifted off my shoulders. My mission to help others through community and sports has led me to where I am and will continue to guide my purpose.” Reyes said she wanted to lead by example. She said she hired an intern who is the daughter of a single mother and is active in sports. Reyes also created what she described as the first scholarship for a nonprofit in Boca Raton, called the LeLa V Leadership Scholarship. The scholarship supports student athletes from low-income households. The award ceremony is scheduled for early next year. Ultrarunners compete in distances longer than a standard 26.2-mile marathon, typically in events ranging from 50 kilometers to 100 miles. More information is available at ErikaReyes.com and lelavsport.com

V, whose given name is Kim Taehyung, is a singer/songwriter known for his distinctive low-pitched voice. He also collaborated with Bing Crosby on a duet version of “White Christmas” in 2024. He has more than 76 million followers on Instagram. Champion, which was founded in 1919, was acquired by Authentic from HanesBrands for $1.2 billion last year. An example of V’s popularity was evident when Jamie Salter, founder and executive chairman of Authentic, ran into the singer at the World Cup finals at MetLife Stadium last month and posted what became a viral shot on his Instagram page. After starting off 2026 with handwritten letters to some of their most devoted fans, confirming their imminent comeback, the biggest band in the world dropped Arirang, their feverishly anticipated fifth studio album, in March, entering the Billboard charts at No. 1 and handily setting a record for the highest sales week for a group in over a decade. Soon after, the band members embarked on their blockbuster Arirang world tour, playing to sold-out stadiums all over the world. And just two weeks ago, they once again dominated headlines, announcing that they won’t submit music to next year’s Grammys, following the Recording Academy’s controversial announcement that it would include an Asian pop music performance category. But despite a busy year for OT7, the members—RM, Jin, Suga, J-Hope, Jimin, V, and Jung Kook—have also managed to pursue their own projects, flaunting the distinctiveness that has always endeared fans to the group. Today, V announces his global partnership with the iconic American sportswear brand Champion, in a campaign called “True Champion” that the company says highlights personalities shaping contemporary culture through their “originality, perspective and enduring impact.” The singer calls the brand “a natural fit,” with the values of the campaign personally resonating with him. “To me, being a ‘True Champion’ isn’t about trying to become someone special,” he says. “Just don’t try too hard to be someone else. I think the more you stay true to yourself, the more confident you’ll become.” V—who has been immersed in the fashion world through his presence at industry events and work with luxury brands—says partnering with Champion is perfectly in line with his life off duty. “I’ve always enjoyed mixing different styles instead of sticking to just one. High fashion is exciting, but I also appreciate clothes that feel effortless to wear,” he says. “When I’m at home, I’m usually dressed even more casually than people would think. I spend a lot of time in simple T-shirts and comfortable clothes because I like feeling relaxed. That’s probably why Champion has always felt familiar to me—it fits naturally into the way I actually dress when I’m off camera.” The campaign also hints at the singer’s passion for music and analog culture, featuring images of him playing the trumpet and standing beside a tower of cassettes. It’s an aspect of his personality that perhaps shone most clearly on his 2023 EP Layover, an intimate, low-key collection of jazz-inflected R&B. “There’s a certain warmth and nostalgia to analog culture, and I’m naturally drawn to that feeling,” he explains. “Vinyl is a good example. Even though Bluetooth speakers are convenient and sound great, I still prefer listening to vinyl records because the whole experience feels more personal and meaningful.” In a Vogue Japan interview from early this year, V talked about gravitating toward the color red. “I always try to include a hint of red [in my outfits],” he said. True enough, one of his Champion items follows that style rule: “My favorite is the gray long-sleeve shirt with the red Champion logo,” he says. “I really liked how the red stands out nicely against the gray and adds just the right pop of color. It’s casual, but the logo gives it just enough character.” Toward the end of the shows on the Arirang world tour, OT7 changes into casual clothes for the last section of the concert, highlighting the distinct personalities and the dynamic that have made the group so compelling. V’s own style has grown by leaps and bounds through the years. “Being in this industry, I’ve had the privilege of working with many different brands and seeing a wide range of styles over the years,” he says. “I’ve learned a lot from just looking at their collections and figuring out what works best for me, and that’s where I get much of my inspiration.” All of that sartorial experimentation has helped him land on a firmer sense of self. “My style is pretty instinctive,” he says. “I just go with whatever catches my eye and wear what feels right. title: Comu is a $6 tiny CH32V203 RISC-V development board that fits inside a USB port - CNX Software
content: Reviews, tutorials and the latest news about embedded systems, IoT, open-source hardware, SBC's, microcontrollers, processors, and more Over the years, we have seen several tiny “omu” USB boards that share this “fits-in-a-USB-port” form factor. It started with the Tomu, based on a Silicon Labs EFM32 Cortex-M0+, followed by the Fomu with a Lattice iCE40 FPGA, Qomu with an EOS S3 Cortex-M4F MCU and FPGA, and the Somu, a tiny FIDO2 security key. Icy Electronics has now introduced Comu, another tiny development board based on the 144 MHz WCH CH32V203 RISC-V MCU. While measuring just 13 x 9.4 mm (slightly smaller than a microSD card), the board still packs two white LEDs, four capacitive touch buttons, and six GPIOs exposed through test pads. It is designed for bare-metal programming, custom USB HID projects, and USB packet experimentation. On the software side, the Comu development board is designed for lightweight bare-metal C/C++ development and works well with the ch32fun project. The developer says a basic blinky program can be as small as 40 bytes. It also comes with a custom 2KB USB bootloader, which leaves about 28KB of boot flash available for user applications. The CH32V203 can also be programmed with Rust (ch32-hal), the Arduino IDE (arduino_core_ch32), or WCH-HAL through the MounRiver Studio IDE. The project is also fully open source, with the KiCad hardware files, custom bootloader, and several example programs available on its GitHub repository. The code samples cover features such as touch sensing, printf, and USB HID/MSC. Besides opening the project in KiCad, you can also check out the PCB layout directly on your web browser on the kicanvas website. The Comu board is currently available on Tindie for $5.99, which includes the white 3D-printed case. Alternatively, you’ll also find it on Lectronz for $5.88.
